QF.id: AIFM CIII Governance and Due Diligence_35

question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund (Cat III AIF, open-ended, daily NAV) receives a grievance from Ms. Priya Shah on 1 May 2026 about delay in redemption settlement. The Manager submits its ATR on SCORES on 18 May 2026. The investor requests first review on 25 May 2026, but feels the revised ATR is inadequate. Within how many calendar days of receiving the revised ATR can the investor approach SEBI for a SECOND review, and what happens meanwhile?

answer.text: Within 15 calendar days; SEBI may take cognizance and intervene; the complaint is resolved/disposed/closed only when SEBI 'disposes' or 'closes' it on SCORES.
Within 365 calendar days; the ATR stands finally resolved after the first review.
Only at AGM; SEBI has no role.
Never — Cat III investors cannot request a second review.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Chapter 11.3.7, an investor may request a SECOND review within 15 calendar days of receiving the revised ATR. SEBI may take cognizance via SCORES and intervene; the AIF must submit revised ATR within SEBI's timeline. Complaint is 'resolved/disposed/closed' only when SEBI itself closes it on SCORES. The Trap: The other options misstate the timeline/outcome or contradict the SEBI Facilitation Regulations. Cross-Exam Context: Same escalation across XIX-C/D. ODR is a parallel route; investor may switch at any time (treated as 'disposed' on SCORES). Manager's Pro-Tip: Pair the SCORES process with proactive Cat III daily-NAV operational controls: settlement delays are the single largest source of investor complaints in open-ended Cat III funds. A T+1 settlement monitoring dashboard that flags PB delays, RTGS failures or NAV-cut-off breaches materially reduces grievance inflow.
